pr_snapshot.body:
ARM DenoiseLuma16 validates all three spans, then checks row slices again for every SIMD load/store. Reuse those validated windows for exact 16-byte anchored pointer access. Preserve arithmetic, signed saturation, correction/decision logic, unaligned/minimal windows, aliases and copy/store order.

Native Apple M4 Max, Go1.27.2 SIMD, PGO off, six balanced confirmation rounds:
- Public DenoiserFilterY improves 1.554x smooth, 1.372x mixed, 1.424x saturating versus the PR29 source, all six pairs faster. Every smooth pair exceeds 1.5x (minimum1.533x), so retain the correctness-verified component gain independently of whole-codec timing.
- Smooth is 1.199x faster than assembly. Mixed/saturating are 14.134x/13.308x faster than assembly, with most of those larger gains predating this change.
- Whole VP8 is mixed: 300 frames +0.391% versus parent (3/6 faster), 60 frames -0.714% (5/6 faster). Current still takes 11.547%/8.317% more time than assembly. All23 non-timing fields match; zero allocations. No general whole-codec speedup or ARM-gap closure is claimed.

Ordinary and native race/checkptr2 denoiser checks pass18 tests each without skips. New84 direct handled/scalar comparisons cover unaligned minimal spans, unequal-stride MC/signal overlaps, both decisions and full-buffer canaries;21 one-byte-short declines preserve buffers. Existing boundary/correction/alias cases pass. Generated function has zero calls/panic paths after the original validation. PGO profile/fingerprint and source/build-selection gates refreshed.

Keep exact sources, initial+fresh kernel rounds, whole timings, correctness, codegen and rejected designs under the dated ARM `denoiser-windows` baseline directory. Preserve the bounded-SSE repeat separately as unselected: no new1.5x gain, consistent with earlier reports. README unchanged. AMD production source is unchanged; fresh x64 CI results are controls.

Fresh native x64 CI controls (AMD production unchanged), EPYC 9V74, Go 1.27.2, PGO off, six paired rounds versus merged main `ed00fc3b` and old assembly `691cd051`:
- Whole VP8 takes 1.188% less time than main (5/6 pairs faster), but still 12.043% more time than assembly in every pair. VP9 320 is -1.096% versus main (5/6 faster), VP9 720 +0.004% (4/6 faster); they take 41.061%/48.141% less time than assembly. These are unchanged-source AMD controls; do not attribute them to the ARM kernel or claim closure of the x64 VP8 gap.
- AMD denoiser smooth/mixed/saturating controls are -0.046%/-0.040%/+0.026% versus main, each 3/6 pairs faster. Preserve all 52 median-regressing kernels; none are slower in all six pairs. The largest is the unchanged SAD16x16 control, +1.583% (4/6 slower).
- All 114 kernel cases have six samples per variant and zero B/op/allocs. Targeted validation passes 73 top-level tests and six retained panic child probes (79 checks; 101 PASS lines including older subtests), with no failures/skips and main/current SIMD dispatch confirmed. All 22 semantic fields match across three public and two profile datasets. Every allocation sample matches its dataset; no allocation outliers this run.

The optimized-C job runs separately on EPYC 9V45 with pinned libvpx v1.16.0, runtime dispatch, SSE2/AVX2 and assembly objects enabled. Fixed-speed VP8 takes 2.174x libvpx time (10.810 versus 4.973 ms/input), with matching measured PSNR/SSIM/payload/encoded and dropped counts. This measured agreement does not assert bitstream identity. Adaptive VP8 is +59.688% and VP9 +174.932%/+171.797%, with unequal quality/output work. All quality-pass output statistics match timed outputs; reference timing uses vpxenc statistics. No comparison across separate CPU jobs or attribution to the ARM source change is intended.

All three exact-head CI checks pass. Raw artifacts: [native](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39063148181/artifacts/12112865648), [optimized C](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39063148181/artifacts/12111769887).
